reasons: Errors are caught and shown as toast messages, which is good.
No tests or other evidence of correct behavior are visible in this file.
Several buttons and the weekly progress display are placeholders with no real behavior.
Frequency is hardcoded to once daily, so other schedules cannot be set here.

used_by: Next.js route for the dashboard reminders page (apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/reminders)

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and shared tools
sections.what: Brings in the icons, reusable card and button pieces, the drawer, the notification helper and the API helper that this page needs.
sections.why: Standard setup so the page can draw its layout and talk to the backend.

sections.name: UIReminder
sections.title: Shape of one reminder on screen
sections.what: Defines the fields each reminder card needs: an id, the database id, type, title, subtitle, time and status (pending, completed or snoozed).
sections.why: Gives one common shape for medicines, water and meals so one card component can show all of them.
sections.watch_out: The status has only three values. A new status from the backend would not be displayed correctly.

sections.name: RemindersPage (part 1)
sections.title: Loading and merging today's reminders
sections.what: Fetches active reminders and builds one list from medicines, the water goal and meals. Each item's status comes from the most recent matching log.
sections.why: The backend sends these as separate groups, and the screen shows them as one daily schedule.
sections.watch_out: Logs are matched only by reminder id, not by date, so whether a log belongs to today depends on the backend sending only today's logs.

sections.name: RemindersPage (part 2)
sections.title: Meal reminders and marking taken or undone
sections.what: Adds meal reminders to the list, then handles the taken button. Pressing it on a completed item sends SKIPPED to undo. Errors reload the list and show a message.
sections.why: The same button both completes and undoes, so the user can correct a mistake. Reason for using SKIPPED to undo is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Undo is saved as SKIPPED, which a backend report might count differently from a reminder never acted on.

sections.name: RemindersPage (part 3)
sections.title: Snoozing and deleting reminders
sections.what: Snooze marks the reminder as snoozed and tells the user it is 15 minutes. Delete removes the reminder from the backend and reloads the list.
sections.why: Snooze lets the user postpone a dose. Delete lets them remove reminders they no longer want.
sections.watch_out: The 15 minute snooze is only a message. The code does not schedule a new alert, so the time is not enforced here.

sections.name: RemindersPage (part 4)
sections.title: Saving a new reminder
sections.what: Checks the form for the chosen category, sends it to the matching backend address, shows a result message, closes the drawer and reloads. It then clears some of the form fields.
sections.why: One save button handles medicine, meal and water reminders, which keeps the drawer simple.
sections.watch_out: The reset clears medicine name, dosage, instructions and meal notes, but not the time or water fields, so old values remain when a new form opens.

sections.name: RemindersPage (part 5)
sections.title: Page header and category picker
sections.what: Shows the title, a settings button that does nothing, and the Add Reminder button. The drawer lets the user choose medication, water goal or meal time.
sections.why: Gives a clear entry point for adding a reminder.
sections.watch_out: The settings button has no click action.

sections.name: RemindersPage (part 6)
sections.title: Medicine form fields
sections.what: Shows fields for medicine name, dosage, meal relation (before, after, with, empty stomach or any time), scheduled time and special instructions.
sections.why: These are the details the backend needs to build a medicine reminder.
sections.watch_out: The form does not collect a frequency. The save sends once daily every time.

sections.name: RemindersPage (part 7)
sections.title: Meal form fields
sections.what: Shows fields for meal type (breakfast, lunch, snack, dinner), scheduled time and dietary notes.
sections.why: These are the details needed for a meal reminder.

sections.name: RemindersPage (part 8)
sections.title: Water goal form fields
sections.what: Shows fields for daily goal in millilitres, interval in minutes, start and end times, and glass size.
sections.why: These let the user set up a repeating water reminder.
sections.watch_out: Numbers are converted with parseInt. An empty or invalid entry becomes NaN and is sent to the backend.

sections.name: RemindersPage (part 9)
sections.title: Drawer footer and today's progress card
sections.what: Shows Cancel and Save Reminder buttons at the bottom of the drawer. Then shows today's adherence card with a percentage bar and a row of four day markers.
sections.why: The footer gives the normal choices. The progress card gives the user a quick sense of how the day is going.
sections.watch_out: The four day markers are fixed in the code (first three ticked), so they do not show real history.

sections.name: RemindersPage (part 10)
sections.title: Daily timeline of reminder cards
sections.what: Lists today's reminders in order with a coloured dot, the card itself, and a delete button that appears when the mouse is over the row. Shows a loading message or a 'no reminders' message when needed.
sections.why: Puts each reminder in a timeline so the user can act on it in sequence.
sections.watch_out: The list is shown in the order the backend sends it. The code does not sort by time.

sections.name: RemindersPage (part 11)
sections.title: Side panel for notifications and calendar
sections.what: Shows Quiet Mode and Critical Alerts as tappable rows, and a Sync with Calendar card with an Enable Sync button.
sections.why: Points the user to extra features planned for the schedule.
sections.watch_out: None of these controls do anything yet. A user may think quiet hours or calendar sync are active.

summary: The Your Schedule page where a user sees today's medicine, water and meal reminders, marks them taken or snoozed, and adds new ones through a drawer form.
purpose: Gives the user one daily checklist for medicines, meals and water, and shows how much of today's list is done.
why: Reason not fully stated in the code. The page is built so the user can act on each reminder without leaving the screen and see progress at a glance.
how: On load, it fetches active reminders from the backend and turns medicines, water goal and meals into one list. Each action (taken, undo, snooze, delete) updates the screen first, then sends the change to the backend, and reloads the list if the save fails. New reminders are created from a drawer with one form per category.
inputs: Reminder data from the GET call to /reminders/active. The user's clicks and form entries for medicine name, dosage, time, meal relation, instructions, meal type, meal time, dietary notes, daily water goal, interval, active hours and glass size.
outputs: A list of reminder cards with a status of pending, completed or snoozed, a progress percentage, and success or error messages. Changes are sent to the backend through POST, PATCH and DELETE calls.
risks: Several controls look live but do nothing: Quiet Mode, Critical Alerts, Calendar Sync, the settings button and the Today button. The weekly progress dots are fixed in the code, not calculated from history. Frequency is always set to once daily when a medicine is saved.
debug: If the list is empty or wrong, check the response from /reminders/active first, especially the logs array and how reminderId matches. If an action seems to revert, look at the error toast text, which shows the backend message. If a new reminder does not appear, check the POST call and then the reload after save.
